Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Digital Code (2025) explicitly grants individuals comprehensive rights to their personal data including right to access a copy, right to rectification, right to erasure and right to data portability, all exercisable free of charge.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Djibouti's Digital Code (Loi n°019/AN/23/9ème L, adopted 30 June 2025, published in the Journal Officiel) establishes a general right of access to personal data (Arts. 32-33) exercisable free of charge (Art. 22), which the techhiveadvisory.africa review correctly summarises; verified against the official gazette text. Note this is a general data-protection right, not evidence of an ID-specific self-service portal, but it satisfies the binary Yes/No scale, so the original code of 2 (Yes) is confirmed, not changed.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration is mandatory in Djibouti at point-of-sale using a valid ID such as a passport or national ID. Djibouti Telecom (state-owned monopoly) requires ID-based registration. This is enshrined in national practice.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original code (2, 'accepted but not mandatory') contradicts the row's own Comments, which state registration is mandatory, and the fandom wiki source cited is a weak, unofficial aggregator. Verified against Décret n°2020-150/PR/MI (2020), Article 8 of which legally requires telecom records to bear the National Identification Number (NNI), Djibouti's foundational ID credential, and against multiple 2023-2025 consumer sources confirming passport/ID presentation is compulsory at point of sale for Djibouti Telecom, the sole operator. Recalculated to 3 (Mandatory) per the scale, since the evidence shows ID-based registration is a legal requirement, not merely accepted practice.
